title: AWS workload sublocation scopes (VPC endpoint, VPC, account, namespace)

prose.text: Workload sublocations are the sublocations created for Cloud Connector workloads, and they differ from ordinary ones in several ways. {{scope-types-and-availability}} {{discovery-required}} {{account-ids-field}}
Their default Workload type and group are in [[zia.locations.group-assignment]]. Ordinary sublocation IP rules are in [[zia.locations.ip-scoping]].

scope-types-and-availability.statement: A sublocation scope segregates workload traffic from one sublocation so different Cloud Connector and ZIA policies apply. It exists only for Workload-type sublocations whose parent location is tied to AWS Cloud Connector groups, with scope types Namespace, Account, VPC and VPC Endpoint (`NAMESPACE`, `ACCOUNT`, `VPC`, `VPC_ENDPOINT` in Terraform's `sub_loc_scope`).

quotes: Scope: You can define scope types to segregate workload traffic from a single sublocation to apply different Zscaler Cloud Connector and security policies.
This field is only available for the Workload traffic type sublocations whose parent locations are associated with Amazon Web Services (AWS) Cloud Connector groups.

* `sub_loc_scope` - (Strings) Defines a scope for the sublocation from the available types to segregate workload traffic from a single sublocation to apply different Cloud Connector and ZIA security policies.

discovery-required.statement: The VPC, Namespace and Account scope types need workload discovery enabled for the tenant; the VPC Endpoint scope type does not.

quotes: To configure sublocations with the VPC, Namespace, and Account scope types, the workload discovery service must be enabled for the tenant. However, it is not required for configuring the VPC Endpoint scope type.

same-criteria-in-a-location.statement: Every sublocation within one location must use the same criteria: scope only, scope plus IP address range, or IP address range only.

quotes: All sublocations within a location must be configured with the same criteria: scope only, combination of scope and IP address range, or IP address range only.

overlap-allowed-across-scopes.statement: Duplicate or overlapping IP address ranges within the same namespace are supported when the subnets sit in separate sublocations (stated for the distributed VPC endpoint model), so policy lookup can tell apart workloads that share an address space.

quotes: In a distributed VPC endpoint deployment, there is one VPC endpoint or a set of VPC endpoints for each subnet or VPC.
Duplicate or overlapping IP address ranges within the same namespace are supported if the subnets are in separate sublocations.
Policy lookup can distinguish between multiple workloads with the same source IP address space, even without using namespace tags or workload discovery.

overlap-allowed-across-scopes.conditions: This is the scoped-workload case; it does not relax the non-overlap rule for ordinary sublocations (see zia.locations.ip-scoping).

hub-vpc-only.statement: In a centralized VPC endpoint deployment a sublocation can be based on the hub VPC but not on the spoke VPCs; the hub VPC can be combined with a unique IP range for finer sublocations.

quotes: In a centralized VPC endpoint deployment, all workload traffic from subnets in spoke VPCs is routed to Cloud Connectors through a shared set of VPC endpoints in a hub VPC. You can create a sublocation based on the hub VPC, but not the spoke VPCs.
However, you can use both the hub VPC and a unique IP address range to create more granular sublocations.

no-authentication.statement: Authentication is not supported for Workload traffic type sublocations.

quotes: The Authentication feature is not supported for the Workload traffic type sublocations.

scope-value-limits.statement: A scoped sublocation holds at most 10 namespace values, 10 account values, 50 VPC values and 50 VPC endpoint values.

quotes: | Namespace Scope per Sublocation 10 scope values | 10 scope values |
| Account Scope per Sublocation | 10 scope values |
| VPC Scope per Sublocation | 50 scope values |
| VPC Endpoint Scope per Sublocation | 50 scope values |

account-ids-field.statement: `sub_loc_acc_ids` lists the AWS account IDs associated with the parent location of a sublocation created in the Cloud & Branch Connector Admin Portal.

quotes: * `sub_loc_acc_ids` - (List of Strings) Specifies one or more Amazon Web Services (AWS) account IDs.
These AWS accounts are associated with the parent location of this sublocation created in the Zscaler Cloud & Branch Connector Admin Portal.

scope-added-to-ip-range.statement: Combining a scope with an IP address range makes sublocations more granular, and a scope can be added to existing sublocations that already have an IP address range.

quotes: Combining a scope and IP address range allows you to create more granular sublocations. You can add a scope to existing sublocations that already have a defined IP address range.

scope-fields-outside-aws.title: Effect of scope fields on non-workload or non-AWS sublocations
scope-fields-outside-aws.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Using these fields on non-workload or non-AWS sublocations has no defined effect." The help states only that the field is available for Workload sublocations of AWS Cloud Connector parents; whether the API rejects, ignores or stores scope values elsewhere is not stated. Resolve with a lab call.
